findings.finding: Setting the repository-level `expected_files` to an empty list removes the default scope contract for every change in this repo, not just G0-01. The residual risk is real: any change that arrives without a task-specific policy under `.diffcipline/tasks/<task-id>.toml` is now bounded only by `forbidden_surfaces` and the line/file ceilings, so unexpected product or plan files could slip through unplanned. This is acknowledged in evidence/g0-01/reconciliation.md, but it is still a global reduction in the guardrail. Consider keeping a minimal fallback contract (or enforcing that a task policy is mandatory via an org-controlled path) so changes without an explicit scope still fail closed.

The offline proof runs with `--require-hashes`, but the `wheel` build backend is only supplied as an un-hashed bootstrap wheel via the extra `--find-links "$bootstrap_dir"` — it never appears as a hashed line in `requirements/locks/linux-amd64-py312.txt` (only `setuptools==84.0.0` is pinned there). Installing the two sdist artifacts from the wheelhouse (`pyzk==0.9`, `svglib==1.5.1`) requires building them, and pip's hash-checking mode applies to build dependencies, so pip will refuse to install `wheel` without a hash and the proof fails. Add a hashed `wheel==0.47.0 --hash=sha256:212281cab4dff978f6cedd499cd893e1f620791ca6ff7107cf270781e587eced` entry to the lock (or pre-install setuptools+wheel with hashes into the venv and use `--no-build-isolation`).

`rm -rf "$run_dir"` deletes a caller-supplied path with no guard. A mis-supplied value (empty string, `/`, or an unintended mount point) would recursively delete arbitrary data inside the builder image. Consider validating that `run_dir` is a non-empty, dedicated subdirectory under a known work root before the destructive cleanup.

With `set -e` active and no error trap, a failure in `python -m venv`, the `pip install`, `pip check`, `license-inventory`, or `verify` step exits the script before this final `cp`, leaving `proof_dir` empty — exactly the case where these logs are needed to diagnose the failure. Consider copying the logs in a `trap ... EXIT` handler (or at least preserving `install.log` even when a later step fails).

`parse_lock()` reads the lock with `path.read_text()` directly, and `cmd_verify()` builds the inventory via `item["name"]`/`item["version"]` without checking each installed entry is a dict with those keys. A missing lock file raises `FileNotFoundError`, and a malformed `installed.json` raises `KeyError`/`TypeError`; `main()` only catches `ToolError`, so these inputs produce a raw traceback instead of the `lockfile:` diagnostic used everywhere else in this module. Consider converting these failures to `ToolError` (as `read_json()` already does).

Adding `docs/qdrat/plan/**` to the repository-level `forbidden_surfaces` makes the earlier claim that "the plan-only contract ... is unchanged in docs/qdrat/plan/plan-policy.toml" misleading. `plan-policy.toml` still declares `expected_files = ["docs/qdrat/plan/**", ...]`, but because repository-level forbidden surfaces are enforced in addition to any task policy (as the comment states), every planning change that edits `docs/qdrat/plan/**` will now be rejected before its own policy applies. The retained `[verification] r1_commands` also point at this now-sealed surface. If sealing the plan is intended, consider reflecting that in `plan-policy.toml` (or documenting where the explicit reconciliation path is expressed) so the two policies don't contradict each other.

findings.existing_code: r2_commands = ["python docs/qdrat/plan/validate_plan.py", "python docs/qdrat/plan/test_validate_plan.py", "python -m unittest discover -s requirements/tests -p test_*.py", "python requirements/tools/lockfile.py verify --target linux-amd64-py312 --lock requirements/locks/linux-amd64-py312.txt --artifacts requirements/artifacts/linux-amd64-py312.json --installed evidence/g0-01/installed.json --tool-distribution pip"]
findings.finding: The unittest pattern `-p test_*.py` is unquoted. If Diffcipline executes this through a shell and any file matching `test_*.py` ever appears in the working directory, the shell will expand the glob before unittest receives it, breaking discovery. Elsewhere in the repo this pattern is quoted (`-p "test_*.py"` in requirements/README.md and evidence/g0-01/README.md). Quote it here as well for consistency, after confirming the executor's shell behavior.

findings.existing_code:
if [ "$run_dir" = "/" ]; then
    echo "acquire: refusing to use / as run_dir" >&2
    exit 2
fi

rm -rf "$run_dir"
findings.suggested_code:
if [ "$(readlink -f -- "$run_dir" 2>/dev/null || echo /)" = "/" ]; then
    echo "acquire: refusing to use / as run_dir" >&2
    exit 2
fi

rm -rf "$run_dir"
findings.finding: The run-dir guard rejects only non-absolute paths and the literal `/`. Equivalent root paths still pass: `//` (which the kernel treats as `/`), `/tmp/..`, `/.`, or `/work/../..`. After passing the `/*` case, `rm -rf "$run_dir"` would then recursively delete `/`, including the bind-mounted `/repo` and `/work`. Normalize the path (or reject `..` components and doubled slashes) before deleting, so the documented safety boundary actually holds.

findings.existing_code:
for item in artifacts["distributions"]:
            artifact = wheelhouse / item["filename"]
findings.finding: `artifact_filename()` takes the URL path basename before `unquote`, so an encoded traversal like `..%2fsecret` decodes to `../secret`. `cmd_verify()` then joins it directly onto the wheelhouse (`wheelhouse / item["filename"]`) with no containment check, so a crafted inventory entry can make verification resolve and hash a file outside the wheelhouse (and leak its sha256 via the mismatch error). Add a containment check before hashing each artifact.

`cmd_build()` compares the two resolutions by whole-list equality but does not re-validate that `normalized_name` values are unique (or that required fields exist) in the winning document. `cmd_resolve()` enforces uniqueness, but `_resolution_distributions()` accepts any schema-valid file. If both inputs contain identical duplicate-named entries, `first == second` passes and duplicates are emitted into both the lock (which `parse_lock()` then rejects) and the inventory (where `cmd_verify()`'s dict comprehension silently collapses them last-wins). Re-validate uniqueness before rendering, so build fails cleanly instead of producing a lock/inventory pair that its own verify step cannot reconcile.

findings.existing_code: r2_commands = ["python docs/qdrat/plan/validate_plan.py", "python docs/qdrat/plan/test_validate_plan.py", "python -m unittest discover -s requirements/tests -p test_*.py", "python requirements/tools/lockfile.py verify --target linux-amd64-py312 --lock requirements/locks/linux-amd64-py312.txt --artifacts requirements/artifacts/linux-amd64-py312.json --installed evidence/g0-01/installed.json --tool-distribution pip"]
findings.finding: The `lockfile.py verify` step omits `--wheelhouse` (and `--bootstrap-dir`), so this reproducible R2 gate reports `verified_artifacts: 0` (see evidence/g0-01/diffcipline-run.log). `cmd_verify` only re-hashes artifacts when `--wheelhouse` is supplied; without it the gate checks lock↔inventory↔installed consistency but never verifies a single artifact's bytes. For a dependency-freeze task, a consistently tampered sha256 in both the lock file and the artifacts JSON would still pass this gate, because the only byte-level check is the acquisition-time `--wheelhouse` run recorded in evidence but not reproducible from the committed policy. Consider documenting this limitation in the task policy, or adding `--wheelhouse`/`--bootstrap-dir` when the artifacts are available in the verification environment.

`run_dir` is guaranteed to start with `/` by the preceding case block, so `"/$run_dir/"` always begins with `//` (e.g. `/work/thing` becomes `//work/thing/`). The `*//*` pattern therefore matches every absolute path, and the script rejects all valid inputs with the "must be a canonical path" error instead of proceeding. Append only a trailing slash so the root case (`/` -> `//`) is still caught while normal paths survive the check.

Listing lines are raw filesystem names produced by `sha256sum ./*` (e.g. `./foo.whl`), not URLs, so applying `unquote` here double-decodes them. A wheel whose on-disk filename contains a literal percent-encoded-looking sequence (because the URL encoded the `%` as `%25`) would be decoded into a different name and then fail the comparison against `recorded`, which uses the raw `item["filename"]`. Keep only `Path(name).name` to strip the `./` prefix.

coverage_limitation.note: OCR default path and extension rules exclude the frozen lock file and the contract test suite, the two artifacts most central to this task. The reviewing agent read both during its own investigation, but that is not the same as reviewing them. Carried forward as QDRAT-REVIEW-RULES-LOCKFILES.

follow_ups: QDRAT-GOV-TASK-POLICY-MANDATORY: make a task-specific Diffcipline policy mandatory through an organisation-controlled (CI) enforcement path rather than by convention.
QDRAT-REVIEW-RULES-LOCKFILES: extend the review rule set so frozen lock files and contract test suites are first-class review targets instead of default exclusions.
verdict: Four rounds, thirteen findings, none open against the frozen artifacts. Every actionable finding was fixed and re-reviewed; the remaining items are one accepted residual governance risk with a named successor, two recorded follow-ups, and one coverage limitation. Round 4 returned no findings, which is where the review loop was closed.
